summary: Built the LEGACY-NEXT static-export adapter (react-next-static-adapter.ts): analyzer-driven, binding-resolved lifts for next/head, next/link, type-only next and next/app, plus getStaticProps carried into a synthesized entry; every other Next surface is a named refusal. Added the next/babel preset translation that recovers the @emotion/react JSX importSource. Ran both lanes twice: era lane is honestly red on byte-stability (random Next build id, deterministic modulo it), migrated Vite 8 lane is byte-stable, no closure install needed (era lockfile rides), 24/24 public assets byte-identical, 8 application files changed. Eight recorded differences published. tsc, lint, and all 1362 node tests green.
open_questions: The @emotion/babel-plugin is not reproduced. Its effect on generated class names is unobservable in these artifacts because the migrated lane emits no Emotion CSS at build time; a witness unit would have to settle it in a browser.

The migrated document delivers no application markup. Whether the mounted page matches the era export is exactly the question a witness unit exists to answer, and no build-level evidence can substitute.
